import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re
import os
from collections import defaultdict

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/en_train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/en_test_2.csv")

# Handle missing values in "before" column for mask operations
before_series = train_df["before"].fillna("")

# Build exact lookup: most frequent after per before
mapping = train_df.groupby(["before", "after"]).size().reset_index(name="count")
most_frequent = (
    mapping.sort_values(["before", "count"], ascending=[True, False])
    .groupby("before")
    .head(1)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
before_to_after = dict(zip(most_frequent["before"], most_frequent["after"]))

# Build lookup for abbreviations ending in '.' (to improve fallback)
abrv_training = train_df[before_series.str.endswith(".")].copy()
abrv_lookup = (
    abrv_training.groupby("before")["after"]
    .apply(
        lambda x: x.value_counts().index[0] if len(x.value_counts()) > 0 else x.iloc[0]
    )
    .to_dict()
)


# Helper to convert numbers to words - FIXED version
def digit_to_word(n):
    # Convert input to integer string
    if isinstance(n, float):
        n = str(int(round(n)))
    n = int(str(n).split(".")[0])

    if n == 0:
        return "zero"

    # Define word lists
    ones = ["", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine"]
    teens = [
        "ten",
        "eleven",
        "twelve",
        "thirteen",
        "fourteen",
        "fifteen",
        "sixteen",
        "seventeen",
        "eighteen",
        "nineteen",
    ]
    tens = [
        "",
        "",
        "twenty",
        "thirty",
        "forty",
        "fifty",
        "sixty",
        "seventy",
        "eighty",
        "ninety",
    ]
    # Extended scales to prevent IndexError for large numbers
    scales = [
        "",
        "thousand",
        "million",
        "billion",
        "trillion",
        "quadrillion",
        "quintillion",
    ]

    def three_digit_to_words(num):
        if num == 0:
            return ""
        parts = []
        hundreds = num // 100
        remainder = num % 100

        if hundreds > 0:
            parts.append(ones[hundreds] + " hundred")

        if remainder > 0:
            if remainder < 10:
                parts.append(ones[remainder])
            elif remainder < 20:
                parts.append(teens[remainder - 10])
            else:
                ten_digit = remainder // 10
                unit_digit = remainder % 10
                word = tens[ten_digit]
                if unit_digit > 0:
                    word += "-" + ones[unit_digit]
                parts.append(word)

        return " ".join(parts)

    # Handle large numbers by chunking
    scale_idx = 0
    parts = []
    while n > 0:
        chunk = n % 1000
        if chunk != 0:
            chunk_words = three_digit_to_words(chunk)
            if scale_idx > 0 and scale_idx < len(scales):
                chunk_words += " " + scales[scale_idx]
            parts.append(chunk_words)
        n //= 1000
        scale_idx += 1

    return " ".join(reversed(parts))


# Ordinal conversion for numbers >= 1
def normalize_ordinal(token):
    token_str = str(token)
    num_str = re.sub(r"(st|nd|rd|th)$", "", token_str)
    try:
        num = int(num_str)
    except ValueError:
        return token_str

    if num == 0:
        return "zeroth"

    # Handle small numbers (1-19) directly
    if num < 20:
        small_ordinals = [
            "first",
            "second",
            "third",
            "fourth",
            "fifth",
            "sixth",
            "seventh",
            "eighth",
            "ninth",
            "tenth",
            "eleventh",
            "twelfth",
            "thirteenth",
            "fourteenth",
            "fifteenth",
            "sixteenth",
            "seventeenth",
            "eighteenth",
            "nineteenth",
        ]
        return small_ordinals[num - 1]

    # For numbers >= 20, use digit_to_word and replace last word
    words = digit_to_word(num).split()
    last_word = words[-1]

    # Handle tens
    if last_word in [
        "twenty",
        "thirty",
        "forty",
        "fifty",
        "sixty",
        "seventy",
        "eighty",
        "ninety",
    ]:
        ordinals = {
            "twenty": "twentieth",
            "thirty": "thirtieth",
            "forty": "fortieth",
            "fifty": "fiftieth",
            "sixty": "sixtieth",
            "seventy": "seventieth",
            "eighty": "eightieth",
            "ninety": "ninetieth",
        }
        words[-1] = ordinals[last_word]
        return " ".join(words)

    # Handle compound numbers ending with ones
    if "-" in last_word:
        base, ones_word = last_word.rsplit("-", 1)
        ones_ordinals = {
            "one": "first",
            "two": "second",
            "three": "third",
            "four": "fourth",
            "five": "fifth",
            "six": "sixth",
            "seven": "seventh",
            "eight": "eighth",
            "nine": "ninth",
        }
        if ones_word in ones_ordinals:
            words[-1] = base + "-" + ones_ordinals[ones_word]
            return " ".join(words)

    # Handle hundreds, thousands, etc.
    if last_word == "hundred":
        words[-1] = "hundredth"
    elif last_word == "thousand":
        words[-1] = "thousandth"
    elif last_word == "million":
        words[-1] = "millionth"
    elif last_word == "billion":
        words[-1] = "billionth"
    else:
        words[-1] = words[-1] + "th"
    return " ".join(words)


# Fraction normalization with standard terms for common fractions
FRACTION_TERMS = {
    (1, 2): "one half",
    (1, 4): "one quarter",
    (3, 4): "three quarters",
    (1, 3): "one third",
    (2, 3): "two thirds",
    (1, 5): "one fifth",
    (2, 5): "two fifths",
    (3, 5): "three fifths",
    (4, 5): "four fifths",
    (1, 6): "one sixth",
    (5, 6): "five sixths",
    (1, 8): "one eighth",
    (3, 8): "three eighths",
    (5, 8): "five eighths",
    (7, 8): "seven eighths",
    (1, 10): "one tenth",
}


def normalize_fraction(numerator_str, denominator_str):
    try:
        num = int(numerator_str)
        den = int(denominator_str)
        if den == 0:
            return f"{digit_to_word(num)} over {digit_to_word(den)}"

        # Check for common fractions first
        def gcd(a, b):
            while b:
                a, b = b, a % b
            return a

        g = gcd(abs(num), abs(den))
        num_reduced = abs(num) // g
        den_reduced = abs(den) // g

        # Handle sign
        sign = "minus " if num < 0 else ""

        # Check for common fractions after reduction
        for (n, d), term in FRACTION_TERMS.items():
            if num_reduced == n and den_reduced == d:
                return f"{sign}{term}"

        # Non-common fractions: use numerator + "over" + denominator
        num_word = digit_to_word(num)
        den_word = digit_to_word(den)
        return f"{sign}{num_word} over {den_word}"
    except (ValueError, ZeroDivisionError):
        return f"{digit_to_word(numerator_str)} over {digit_to_word(denominator_str)}"


# Heuristic normalizer with improved fallback
def heuristic_normalize(token):
    token_str = str(token)

    # Punctuation, self, sil
    if token_str in [".", ",", "!", "?", ";", ":", '"', "'", "(", ")"]:
        return token_str
    elif token_str in ["<self>", "sil"]:
        return token_str

    # Fraction detection (X/Y where both X and Y are numeric)
    if re.match(r"^-?\d+/\d+$", token_str):
        parts = token_str.split("/")
        return normalize_fraction(parts[0], parts[1])

    # Ordinal numbers (e.g., 1st, 2nd, 23rd, 100th)
    if re.match(r"^\d+(st|nd|rd|th)$", token_str):
        return normalize_ordinal(token_str)

    # Number → words
    if re.match(r"^[0-9]+$", token_str):
        return digit_to_word(token_str)

    # Decimal numbers (e.g., 3.14)
    if re.match(r"^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$", token_str):
        parts = token_str.split(".")
        integer_part = digit_to_word(parts[0]) if parts[0] else "zero"
        decimal_digits = [digit_to_word(d) for d in parts[1]]
        return integer_part + " point " + " ".join(decimal_digits)

    # Currency (e.g., $3, $3.16)
    if re.match(r"^\$\d+(\.\d+)?$", token_str):
        amt = token_str[1:]
        if "." in amt:
            dollars, cents = amt.split(".")
            d = digit_to_word(dollars) if dollars else "zero"
            c = digit_to_word(cents) if cents else "zero"
            return f"{d} dollars {c} cents"
        else:
            d = digit_to_word(amt) if amt else "zero"
            return f"{d} dollars"

    # Measure units (e.g., 6ft, 150lb)
    if re.match(r"^\d+ft$", token_str):
        num_part = token_str[:-2]
        return digit_to_word(num_part) + " feet"
    if re.match(r"^\d+lb$", token_str):
        num_part = token_str[:-2]
        return digit_to_word(num_part) + " pounds"

    # Time (e.g., 12:47)
    if re.match(r"^\d+:\d{2}$", token_str):
        h, m = token_str.split(":")
        h_word = digit_to_word(h)
        if m == "00":
            return h_word + " hundred"
        elif m[0] == "0":
            return h_word + " oh " + digit_to_word(m[1])
        else:
            return h_word + " " + digit_to_word(m)

    # Common abbreviations ending in '.' (lookup training)
    if token_str.endswith("."):
        return abrv_lookup.get(token_str, token_str.lower())

    # Plain alphabetic (lowercase)
    if token_str.isalpha():
        return token_str.lower()

    # Fallback
    return token_str.lower()


# Generate id column for test set
test_df["id"] = (
    test_df["sentence_id"].astype(str) + "_" + test_df["token_id"].astype(str)
)

# Predict
test_df["prediction"] = test_df["before"].map(before_to_after)
missing_mask = test_df["prediction"].isna()
test_df.loc[missing_mask, "prediction"] = test_df.loc[missing_mask, "before"].apply(
    heuristic_normalize
)

# Save submission
submission = pd.DataFrame({"id": test_df["id"], "after": test_df["prediction"]})
submission.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)

# Validate on stratified hold-out (1% of train, stratified by class to avoid leakage)
val_df = train_df.groupby("class", group_keys=False).apply(
    lambda x: x.sample(frac=0.01, random_state=42)
)
val_df["prediction"] = val_df["before"].map(before_to_after)
missing_mask_val = val_df["prediction"].isna()
val_df.loc[missing_mask_val, "prediction"] = val_df.loc[
    missing_mask_val, "before"
].apply(heuristic_normalize)
accuracy = (val_df["prediction"] == val_df["after"]).mean()

print(f"Validation accuracy (stratified hold-out): {accuracy:.6f}")
